title: Microsoft Edge: automatically unsubscribe users from notifications sent by scam and malicious sites
summary: The briefing's behaviour, rollout details and notification controls are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft documentation. The registry references are correct despite the automated warnings; the low impact rating should be revised because this changes default user behaviour.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Edge automatically stops further notifications from a source when its notification leads to a SmartScreen-blocked scam, phishing or malware page.
claims.quote: When a notification leads users to a site that Microsoft Defender SmartScreen blocks as a scam, phishing, or malware page, Edge automatically stops that source from sending further notifications.

claims.quote: Users can review and restore any of these sites anytime under edge://settings/privacy/sitePermissions/allPermissions/notifications.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No administrator UI or policy/automation switch specific to automatic unsubscribe is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatically unsubscribe malicious scam notifications policy administrator disable licensing price. Read Stable/archived notes, both notification-policy references and policy index; searched index for unsubscribe, notification and SmartScreen.

claims.claim: The Edge 158 release notes list no policy specific to this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatically unsubscribe malicious scam notifications policy administrator disable. Opened and read the Edge 158 Feature Updates and all Policy Updates; none names an automatic-unsubscribe policy.

claims.claim: The roadmap and release notes do not describe how Edge records the unsubscribe decision.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatic unsubscribe notifications restore managed profiles SmartScreen policy data stored approval. Read roadmap and Stable/archived feature entries; they describe the trigger, stopping notifications, informing users and restoration, not decision storage.

claims.claim: The roadmap and release notes do not describe what the user notice looks like.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatic unsubscribe notifications restore managed profiles SmartScreen policy data stored approval. Read roadmap and Stable/archived entries; they say Edge informs users but supply no notice wording or appearance.

claims.claim: Web notification permissions allow a site to reach a user after the user has left its app.
claims.quote: When using the app in either Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, the notification appears even if the user isn't actively using the Blazing Pizza app. However, the browser must be running, or the notification appears the next time that the browser is opened.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's release-note entries do not describe what Edge sends to Microsoft or stores for automatic unsubscribe.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatic unsubscribe notifications restore managed profiles SmartScreen policy data stored approval. Read Stable/archived feature entries and privacy/SmartScreen search excerpts; general reputation-check data is described, not unsubscribe-specific data handling.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The described trigger concerns a notification-led visit to a SmartScreen-blocked destination, not a malicious destination SmartScreen has not blocked.
claims.quote: When a notification leads users to a site that Microsoft Defender SmartScreen blocks as a scam, phishing, or malware page, Edge automatically stops that source from sending further notifications.

claims.claim: Restoring an automatically unsubscribed site allows its notifications again.
claims.quote: Edge automatically stops that source from sending further notifications. Edge also informs users. Users can review and restore these sites anytime under `edge://settings/privacy/sitePermissions/allPermissions/notifications`.

claims.claim: The release notes do not state whether restoring sites is allowed for managed profiles.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatic unsubscribe notifications restore managed profiles SmartScreen policy data stored approval. Read Stable/archived entries and restoration search results; no managed-profile qualification appears.

claims.claim: The release notes describe no user or administrator approval step before automatic unsubscribe.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge automatic unsubscribe notifications restore managed profiles SmartScreen policy data stored approval. Read Stable/archived feature entries: Edge acts automatically, informs users, and permits later restoration; no approval step is described.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: DefaultNotificationsSetting is an existing general control deciding whether websites can display notifications by default.
claims.quote: Set whether websites can display desktop notifications. You can allow them by default ('AllowNotifications'), deny them by default ('BlockNotifications'), or have the user be asked each time a website wants to show a notification ('AskNotifications').

claims.where: controls[2].governs; controls[2].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: NotificationsBlockedForUrls is an existing general control specifying sites that cannot display notifications.
claims.quote: Allows you to create a list of url patterns to specify sites that aren't allowed to display notifications.

claims.claim: The low impact rating fits an automatic change to existing notification behaviour.
claims.quote: impact: "low"; defaultState: "on". Standard: low means "admins only, or a small opt-in group"; high means "most users, or a change to default behaviour".
claims.fix: Set impact to high and replace its rationale with: "High. Edge changes notification behaviour automatically when a notification leads to a SmartScreen-blocked scam, phishing or malware page; affected users do not opt in to this protection."
